scene_translation: The station attendant was sweating a little. "Um... I don't know anything about the lockers," he said. But his eyes were looking toward the lockers. When テスト stepped closer, there was a small piece of paper stuck to the bottom locker. It read: "To テスト."
grammar_note: 【〜てある】e.g.「貼ってある」and「書いてある」— this form means something has been done and the result remains, often intentionally by someone. Different from 〜ている, which describes ongoing action or state.

mystery_memo: The central mystery deepens: someone — almost certainly the woman in blue — left a note addressed specifically to テスト on the locker BEFORE テスト arrived, suggesting she knew he would come. The station attendant (Suzuki, name TBD) is nervous and evasive; he likely knows more but is afraid — relationship: suspicious/uncomfortable. The small note is now in テスト's inventory and will reveal a locker number or cryptic message in the next scene. The lockers themselves may hold a key item.
